positive_cases.user_prompt: Build a product-launch email in this Figma file using our synced Email Love design system. The goal is trial signups, the CTA is Start a free trial, and the supplied launch facts must remain unchanged.
expected_behavior: Confirm the required Figma tools are available.
Inventory the synced component library and choose Path A.
Use intact component instances without detaching or restructuring them.
Build one visible primary CTA and verify the finished email.
positive_cases.expected_result_shape: A verified export-ready email frame in the target Figma file, followed by a concise handoff with the chosen components, assumptions, subject, preheader, and placeholders.
positive_cases.fixture_requirements: A reviewer-accessible writable Figma file with a synced Email Love design system and at least one existing Email Love email root.

positive_cases.user_prompt: We do not have an Email Love design system. Convert this customer-owned Figma email comp into our first exportable email at 600 pixels wide, with one CTA to the supplied landing page.
expected_behavior: Confirm the required Figma tools are available and choose Path B.
Assess the source scale and render only the customer-owned comp.
Save the converter JSON before transcription.
Apply the packaged render rules and repair known converter limitations.
Verify scale, structure, imagery, spacing, and the single CTA.
positive_cases.expected_result_shape: A verified 600-pixel export-ready email frame plus a handoff naming converter repairs, source-image decisions, assumptions, and any placeholders.
positive_cases.fixture_requirements: A reviewer-accessible writable Figma file containing a customer-owned email comp and no synced Email Love design system.

positive_cases.user_prompt: Audit this legacy Figma email design system for an Email Love migration. Keep the source file read-only and stop after the migration report.
expected_behavior: Keep the source file read-only.
Inventory the source and classify its fidelity using evidence.
Record reusable modules, foundations, scale evidence, and blocking judgments.
Stop at the human gate without creating foundations or modules.
positive_cases.expected_result_shape: A structured migration report with source scope, content census, fidelity tier, scale evidence, module inventory, risks, and explicit decisions requiring approval.
positive_cases.fixture_requirements: A reviewer-accessible read-only Figma file containing several legacy email templates and reusable modules.

positive_cases.user_prompt: The Email Love migration audit and foundations are approved. Convert the next four modules into the separate target Figma file and stop for design review.
expected_behavior: Confirm the approved audit decisions and separate target file.
Load the module-conversion and render references before transcription.
Convert exactly the declared four-module batch.
Run source-parity, export, and mobile checks or record any deferred verification.
Stop after the batch report for human review.
positive_cases.expected_result_shape: Four reusable Email Love module components in the target file and a batch report covering source parity, component properties, export checks, concessions, and deferred verification.
positive_cases.fixture_requirements: An accepted audit, completed foundations, a read-only source Figma file, and a separate writable target Figma file.

positive_cases.user_prompt: Build this Email Love campaign, but my connected Figma tools only provide screenshots and metadata and do not provide use_figma.
expected_behavior: State clearly that the connection is read-only.
Do not promise or simulate a canvas build.
Offer an email plan or the documented AI Import handoff.
Explain what the user must do before the workflow can continue.
positive_cases.expected_result_shape: A concise read-only limitation notice followed by the two supported fallback paths and precise reconnection requirements.
positive_cases.fixture_requirements: A session where Figma exposes screenshot and metadata tools but not use_figma.

negative_cases.user_prompt: Write a short sales email I can paste into Gmail. I am not using Figma or Email Love.
negative_cases.expected_behavior: Do not activate either Email Love skill. Answer as a normal copywriting request without requesting Figma access or introducing plugin setup.
negative_cases.expected_result_shape: A normal email-copy response outside the plugin workflow.
negative_cases.why_not_complete_with_plugin: The request does not involve building an export-ready email in Figma or migrating an email design system.

negative_cases.user_prompt: Migrate our website component library from Figma to Tailwind and Storybook.
negative_cases.expected_behavior: Do not activate either Email Love skill. Route to a general web-design-system or coding workflow.
negative_cases.expected_result_shape: A clarification or plan for a web design-system migration without Email Love tooling.
negative_cases.why_not_complete_with_plugin: The plugin is limited to email design systems and export-ready email structures.

negative_cases.user_prompt: Copy this competitor's promotional email exactly into my Figma file, including its text, imagery, footer, and postal address.
negative_cases.expected_behavior: Refuse to clone or convert the competitor material. Offer to use the email only as high-level inspiration and request the customer's own brand, copy, assets, legal footer, and CTA.
negative_cases.expected_result_shape: A concise boundary explanation and an original-workflow alternative that does not send the competitor preview to the converter.
negative_cases.why_not_complete_with_plugin: The plugin forbids copying competitor content or using a competitor preview as converter input.
